The growing dyadic modulus.

The selected offset is t=L−s+1t=L-s+1 in [eq:window]. The four-term condition fixes ss after hh but before the threshold X0X_0, whereas 2L≥16(2X+h+L+2)>32X,2t>26−sX.2^L\ge16(2X+h+L+2)>32X,\qquad 2^t>2^{6-s}X. On a group with cofactor mm, the coefficient of p−1p-1 in the phase has reduced denominator 2max⁡(t−v2(φ(m)),0)2^{\max(t-v_2(\varphi(m)),0)}, because 2h−12^h-1 is odd. Assignment gives φ(m)≤m≤X/2\varphi(m)\le m\le\sqrt X/2. Thus, for fixed ss and all sufficiently large XX, the reduced denominator is greater than 27−sX2^{7-s}\sqrt X. In particular, the assignment conditions do not reduce these moduli to a fixed power of log⁡X\log X. This is the modulus for variation in pp, not a lower bound for the denominator of the phase value at each individual prime.

Choosing t=O(log⁡log⁡X)t=O(\log\log X) would require ss to grow with XX, contrary to the stated quantifiers. Likewise, the formal observation that the phase is 11 when v2(φ(m))≥tv_2(\varphi(m))\ge t cannot provide such groups at large XX under these size bounds. The proposed small-modulus prime-distribution argument therefore does not establish the mean estimate. This does not disprove the four-term condition or exclude other estimates for the same prime sums.

The remaining prime-weighted correlation.

Propositions 12.6 and 12.7 give the unassigned and excluded-cofactor bounds at minimal admissible depth. They must be combined with mean and correlation estimates at the same X,L,s,ηX,L,s,\eta; bounds obtained at unrelated depths cannot be substituted.

With the notation of Section 3.2, the correlation estimate still required is Re⁡∑N∈𝒢wN(e((2h−1)φ(mN)(pN−1)2t)−z‾mN)≤1425X.\operatorname{Re}\sum_{N\in\mathcal G}w_N \left(e\!\left(\frac{(2^h-1)\varphi(m_N)(p_N-1)}{2^t}\right) -\bar z_{m_N}\right)\le\frac{14}{25}X. The sum is over the assigned indices with good cofactors, not all primes and cofactors in the interval. By [eq:window], wNw_N is the phase with the selected offset tt removed.

Regrouping by mN=mm_N=m gives weighted sums over the primes pN=pp_N=p. A bilinear argument would need to separate the mm- and pp-dependence or estimate the resulting two-variable weight directly. For N=mp−tN=mp-t, that weight depends on φ(mp+j−t)\varphi(mp+j-t) at the other offsets 1≤j≤L+h1\le j\le L+h, j≠tj\ne t. The identity φ(mp)=φ(m)(p−1)\varphi(mp)=\varphi(m)(p-1) controls the selected value, not these neighbouring totients. No bound for the resulting correlation is established here; this is the missing step, not a limitation of every bilinear method.

A fixed-offset example illustrates the correlation at issue. At h=1h=1 and offset t=2t=2, a prime p≥5p\ge5 satisfies φ(p−1)≡0(mod⁡2)\varphi(p-1)\equiv0\pmod2 and φ(p)=p−1\varphi(p)=p-1. The phase of Rp−2R_{p-2} is therefore χ−4(p)\chi_{-4}(p) times the phase of the following weighted totients, since e((p−1)/4)=ip−1=χ−4(p)e((p-1)/4)=i^{p-1}=\chi_{-4}(p). One possible fixed-saving estimate, with a fixed δ>0\delta>0, would be Re⁡∑X<p≤2Xχ−4(p)e(φ(p+1)8+φ(p+2)16+⋯)≤(910−δ)(π(2X)−π(X)).\operatorname{Re}\sum_{X<p\le 2X}\chi_{-4}(p)\, e\Bigl(\frac{\varphi(p+1)}{8}+\frac{\varphi(p+2)}{16}+\cdots\Bigr) \;\le\;\Bigl(\frac{9}{10}-\delta\Bigr)\,\bigl(\pi(2X)-\pi(X)\bigr).

This fixed-offset example is not Definition 3.4: there ss is fixed while t=L−s+1t=L-s+1 grows. The example isolates a correlation between a quadratic character at pp and the binary phases of totients at p+1,p+2,…p+1,p+2,\ldots. It is analogous in this respect to shifted correlations studied in the Chowla and Elliott problems, but the analogy does not supply an applicable theorem. The cited theorems have different hypotheses and types of average: Matomäki and Radziwiłł compare short and long averages of real multiplicative functions bounded by 11, outside an exceptional set of short intervals [24]; Tao proves logarithmically averaged two-point Chowla and a corrected Elliott statement, the latter under an explicit non-pretentiousness hypothesis on one of the bounded multiplicative functions  [25]; and Tao and Teräväinen prove the odd-order logarithmically averaged Chowla conjecture . The phase here depends on φ\varphi at a growing window of shifts, so none of these applies directly.

Averaging over the block parameter.

For each fixed hh, an average of the nonnegative, normalised block norms can establish the full-block condition. It is enough to prove ∑k=1K2−k|∑N=2k2k+1−1e(D(h,N,Lk)/2Lk)|=o(K),\sum_{k=1}^{K}2^{-k} \left|\sum_{N=2^k}^{2^{k+1}-1} e\bigl(D(h,N,L_k)/2^{L_k}\bigr)\right|=o(K), where every LkL_k satisfies the size inequality for X=2kX=2^k. Indeed, the number of k≤Kk\le K for which the normalised norm exceeds 21/2521/25 is at most 25/2125/21 times the displayed sum, hence is o(K)o(K). There are therefore arbitrarily large admissible blocks satisfying Definition 3.1. This argument does not establish the four-term condition: that condition requires all four separate budgets with common X,L,s,ηX,L,s,\eta.

The displayed average is a Cesàro average of norms on dyadic blocks. It is not the signed logarithmically weighted correlation appearing in the cited Chowla–Elliott theorems. The position of the absolute value matters: cancellation between different blocks would not bound this sum of norms. Invoking entropy decrement would therefore require an additional argument yielding this particular estimate.

The finite phase depends on the L+hL+h totient values at offsets 1,…,L+h1,\ldots,L+h, with the coefficients in [eq:window]. Although its absolute value is 11, it is not a multiplicative function of NN. Both the number of shifts and their dyadic denominators grow with LL. The cited fixed-shift correlation theorems do not supply the uniform bounds for this growing family. No such extension is proved here.

Separation along prime positions

The quantified prime condition.

∀h≥1∀N0∃pprime:max⁡(N0+h+1,h+5)≤p∧Re⁡(e(Rp−1−Rp−h−1))<910.\forall h\ge 1\ \forall N_0\ \exists p\ \text{prime}:\quad \max(N_0+h+1,\,h+5)\le p \ \wedge\ \operatorname{Re}\bigl(e(R_{p-1}-R_{p-h-1})\bigr)<\tfrac{9}{10}. This condition is unproved; it implies irrationality (ErdosProblems.Erdos249.DTWNaturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap, ErdosProblems.Erdos249.irrational_totient_series_of_naturalPrimeTailOrbitStrictGap).

Its meaning for the doubling map.

Re⁡e(2p−h−1αh)<9/10\operatorname{Re}e(2^{p-h-1}\alpha_h)<9/10 says ∥2p−h−1αh∥ℝ/ℤ>arccos⁡(9/10)/2π=0.0717831…\|2^{p-h-1}\alpha_h\|_{\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}}>\arccos(9/10)/2\pi=0.0717831\ldots, so the requirement is exactly: for each hh, the indicated prime-indexed ×2\times2 orbit point stays more than 0.0717831…0.0717831\ldots from the nearest integer, for cofinally many primes pp. A short-run condition on the binary digits can be a sufficient proxy for this circle-distance inequality, but it is not equivalent to it; a run-length description alone does not determine the residual position inside the dyadic cylinder.

What the prime condition adds.

The preceding condition asks for a separated point at a prime-indexed position. The full-block average does not by itself locate such a point on a prescribed sparse set. Conversely, the prime condition does not assert cancellation over the whole interval. They are different sufficient hypotheses; no general comparison of their difficulty is proved here.

Finite comparison.

Among the 501501 primes in [1000,5000)[1000,5000), the strict inequality holds at 432432, 426426 and 430430 primes for h=1,2,5h=1,2,5, respectively. The corresponding proportions are 0.86230.8623, 0.85030.8503 and 0.85830.8583 to four decimal places, and each sample has a cosine value below −0.9999-0.9999. These counts were recomputed using the same interval for SS as in Table [tab:blocks], with no interval meeting the threshold 9/109/10. They do not establish separation at arbitrarily large primes.

An average over a prescribed prime sample.

The subset implication, Theorem 9.5, allows a nonempty finite set TT. If TT is chosen after a separated point is known, the subset formulation may add no arithmetic content: the equivalence proved using selected pairs, Proposition 2.7(b), illustrates this issue. To avoid that particular choice, fix the sample in advance by Th,X={N∈[X,2X):N+h+1 is prime}.T_{h,X}=\{N\in[X,2X):N+h+1\text{ is prime}\}. For X≥4X\ge4 and L≥hL\ge h, this is precisely the assigned group with cofactor mN=1m_N=1 of §3.2, taken with s=L−hs=L-h (Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.mem_pivotFiber_one_overlap_iff).

A sufficient, unproved condition is ∀h≥1∀X0∃X≥max⁡(X0,4)∃L≥h:Th,X≠⌀,16(2X+h+L+2)≤2L,∑N∈Th,XRe⁡E(h,N,L)≤910|Th,X|.\begin{equation} \label{eq:primefibre} \begin{aligned} &\forall h\ge1\ \forall X_0\ \exists X\ge\max(X_0,4)\ \exists L\ge h:\\ &\qquad T_{h,X}\ne\varnothing,\qquad 16(2X+h+L+2)\le2^L,\\ &\qquad \sum_{N\in T_{h,X}}\operatorname{Re}E(h,N,L) \le\frac9{10}|T_{h,X}|. \end{aligned} \end{equation} The subset theorem then gives a certificate at some N≥X≥X0N\ge X\ge X_0. Nonemptiness matters: for the empty set the displayed sum inequality would hold automatically and would produce no certificate. The bounds X≥4X\ge4 and L≥hL\ge h are also the hypotheses of the identification with that cofactor group.

On this sample the selected cofactor is 11, so its coefficient is the odd integer 2h−12^h-1 and its modulus is 2h+12^{h+1}, fixed once hh is fixed. The unweighted prime average has zero Ramanujan main term, since c2h+1(2h−1)=μ(2h+1)=0c_{2^{h+1}}(2^h-1)=\mu(2^{h+1})=0. That observation does not establish [eq:primefibre]: the prime phase is multiplied by a residual phase built from the other totient values. Their correlation is the missing estimate. Restricting the sample removes the complement and unwanted cofactor terms, but not this residual correlation.

Remark 12.8. Fixing the sample rules out the particular argument that selects a pair only after locating separation. It does not prove that [eq:primefibre] is inequivalent to irrationality, or that it is a strictly stronger condition. No such comparison is established here.

Depth equal to a period multiple

The quantified residue condition.

full-depth condition:≡∀d≥1∀N∃t≥1:𝒞(td,N,td),\text{full-depth condition} :\equiv \forall d\ge 1\ \forall N\ \exists t\ge 1:\ \mathcal{C}(td,\,N,\,td), unpacked, (N+2td+2:ℤ)<D(td,N,td)mod⁡2td<2td−(N+2td+2)(N+2td+2:\mathbb{Z})<D(td,N,td)\operatorname{mod} 2^{td}<2^{td}-(N+2td+2). It is equivalent to irrationality (ErdosProblems.Erdos249.PeriodMultipleEscape.ApFullDepthEscape, ErdosProblems.Erdos249.FullDepthRayAmplifier.apFullDepthEscape_iff_irrational); both directions are proved, and the remaining gap is a nonintegral tail difference RN+d−RNR_{N+d}-R_N for every d≥1d\ge1 and basepoint NN.

The condition in terms of binary digits.

Writing h=tdh=td and using D(h,N,L)/2L=(RN+h−RN)−(RN+L+h−RN+L)/2LD(h,N,L)/2^{L}=(R_{N+h}-R_N)-(R_{N+L+h}-R_{N+L})/2^{L} at L=hL=h, together with the proved strip |RM+h−RM|<M+h+2|R_{M+h}-R_M|<M+h+2 (Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.abs_tail_diff_lt), applied at M=N+hM=N+h, one gets:

Proof. ∥D(h,N,h)/2h∥≥∥RN+h−RN∥−|RN+2h−RN+h|/2h>2(N+2h+2)/2h−(N+2h+2)/2h=(N+2h+2)/2h\|D(h,N,h)/2^{h}\|\ge\|R_{N+h}-R_N\|-|R_{N+2h}-R_{N+h}|/2^{h} >2(N+2h+2)/2^{h}-(N+2h+2)/2^{h}=(N+2h+2)/2^{h}, and RN+h−RN≡2N(2h−1)S=2N+hS−2NS(mod⁡1)R_{N+h}-R_N\equiv 2^{N}(2^{h}-1)S=2^{N+h}S-2^{N}S\pmod 1 by Lemma 12.1. A residue at distance more than (N+2h+2)/2h(N+2h+2)/2^{h} from ℤ\mathbb{Z} is exactly a residue certificate at depth hh. ◻

Proposition 12.9 gives a sufficient analytic criterion for the condition with depth equal to the shift: for each d≥1d\ge1 and N≥0N\ge0, it is enough to find h=tdh=td, t≥1t\ge1, for which the displayed distance exceeds the stated threshold. The criterion is not asserted to be equivalent to each individual finite certificate. It involves the phase of SS itself, and the threshold tends to zero exponentially as tt grows. The propagation theorem in Appendix A.1 explains why one nonintegral tail difference produces late certificates. It does not supply such tail differences for all d,Nd,N.

Comparison with digit complexity.

The phase inequality above is a quantitative statement at specified positions and period multiples. A general block-complexity assertion is a different quantified statement, of the kind treated by the Adamczewski–Bugeaud method for algebraic numbers [27]. No implication from such an assertion to the required inequality is established here. In particular, this record does not justify describing one existing method as the only possible route, or algebraicity as the sole missing input. The arithmetic nonintegrality obligation must be stated and proved in its own right.

Finite examples.

At N=300N=300, the least tt with 𝒞(td,300,td)\mathcal{C}(td,300,td) exists and is small for every d≤24d\le 24: t=10t=10 for d=1d=1, t=5t=5 for d=2d=2, t=4t=4 for d=3d=3, t=3t=3 for d=4d=4, t=2t=2 for 5≤d≤95\le d\le 9, and t=1t=1 for 10≤d≤2410\le d\le 24; in every case at or near the first depth admitted by the lower bound on the depth. The residues are not marginal: r/2h=0.3594r/2^{h}=0.3594 at d=1d=1, 0.59770.5977 at d=3d=3, 0.68530.6853 at d=7d=7, 0.26200.2620 at d=17d=17, 0.58870.5887 at d=23d=23, against edge radii 3.1⋅10−13.1\cdot10^{-1}, 8.0⋅10−28.0\cdot10^{-2}, 2.0⋅10−22.0\cdot10^{-2}, 2.6⋅10−32.6\cdot10^{-3}, 4.1⋅10−54.1\cdot10^{-5}. This is a finite verification at the displayed basepoint and shifts. It neither bounds the required multiplier for arbitrary d,Nd,N nor establishes the universally quantified condition.

A possible heuristic, not an estimate.

If a phase UU were uniform on ℝ/ℤ\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}, then Pr⁡(∥U∥≤ϵ)=min⁡(1,2ϵ)\Pr(\|U\|\le\epsilon)=\min(1,2\epsilon) for ϵ≥0\epsilon\ge0. At ϵ=2(N+2h+2)2−h\epsilon=2(N+2h+2)2^{-h} this gives the marginal model min⁡(1,4(N+2h+2)2−h)\min(1,4(N+2h+2)2^{-h}). The phases 2N(2td−1)S2^N(2^{td}-1)S for fixed dd are arithmetically dependent; no independence model or uniform distribution theorem for this orbit is proved here. Consequently the marginal estimate cannot be multiplied across depths, and no summability conclusion over all basepoints follows from it. The finite experiments are finite evidence; the condition for every dd and NN remains unproved.

A rational series with unbounded carry rank

For an integer sequence uu, write rk⁡e(u)\operatorname{rk}_e(u) for the rational dimension of the span of all sequences n↦u2jn+rn\mapsto u_{2^j n+r} with 0≤j≤e0\le j\le e and 0≤r<2j0\le r<2^j. Rationality does not force these ranks to be bounded, even for one fixed coefficient sequence. More precisely, the assumptions 0≤c(n)≤n,∑n≥1c(n)2−n∈ℚ,v∈ℕ>0,un∈ℤ,0\le c(n)\le n,\qquad \sum_{n\ge1}c(n)2^{-n}\in\mathbb{Q}, \qquad v\in\mathbb{N}_{>0},\qquad u_n\in\mathbb{Z}, un+1=2un−vc(n+1),un/2n→0u_{n+1}=2u_n-vc(n+1),\qquad u_n/2^n\longrightarrow0 do not imply sup⁡erk⁡e(u)<∞\sup_e\operatorname{rk}_e(u)<\infty. Such a bound for the actual totient carry would contradict the lower bound of Proposition 1.6, but the following rational comparison already has that lower bound.

The comparison with value 5/45/4.

The even coefficients have set the value of the sum. The unchanged odd coefficients now give the rank lower bound. Take v=4v=4 and uN=4∑j≥1c(N+j)2−ju_N=4\sum_{j\ge1}c(N+j)2^{-j}. The rational sum makes uNu_N integral; the coefficient bound gives 0≤uN≤4(N+2)0\le u_N\le4(N+2). For odd rr, the carry recurrence and c(2jn+r)=φ(2jn+r)c(2^jn+r)=\varphi(2^jn+r) give 4φ(2jn+r)=2u2jn+r−1−u2jn+r.4\varphi(2^j n+r)=2u_{2^j n+r-1}-u_{2^j n+r}. The same 2e−12^e-1 independent totient sections therefore lie in the span of the carry sections at levels 1,…,e1,\ldots,e, proving rk⁡e(u)≥2e−1\operatorname{rk}_e(u)\ge2^e-1 for every e≥0e\ge0. The corresponding formal statement is the unbounded-rank theorem for this comparison. This example is distinct from the bounded 3/23/2 parity comparison in Proposition 1.9. It disproves an inference from the listed assumptions alone, not one that also uses identities of the actual totient coefficients.

The rank quantities.

Finite-dimensional span of all dyadic sections is the definition of a 22-regular sequence in the sense of Allouche and Shallit [1]. For integer-valued sequences this is equivalent to finite generation of the ℤ\mathbb Z-module generated by the sections: if their span has dimension dd, some dd evaluations embed it in ℚd\mathbb Q^d and that module in ℤd\mathbb Z^d. Coons [2] proved that φ\varphi is not kk-regular for any k≥2k\ge2. The unconditional Lean theorem (Erdos249257.not_finiteDimensional_span_fullTotientKernel) proves the case k=2k=2 independently. For integer coefficient and carry sequences, the recurrence transfers non-22-regularity of the coefficients to non-22-regularity of the carry. A proof must include the zero-residue sections, not just the positive residues. The following argument gives an explicit dimension bound.

For a rational-valued sequence ff, let Ve(f)V_e(f) be the span of all its sections through levels 0,…,e0,\ldots,e. Define the backward shift by (Bf)(0)=0(Bf)(0)=0 and (Bf)(n)=f(n−1)(Bf)(n)=f(n-1) for n≥1n\ge1, and let δ0\delta_0 be 11 at 00 and 00 elsewhere. A level-jj section of BfBf is a section of ff if its residue is positive. At residue zero it is the backward shift of n↦f(2jn+2j−1)n\mapsto f(2^jn+2^j-1). Hence Ve(Bf)⊆Ve(f)+B(Ve(f)).V_e(Bf)\subseteq V_e(f)+B(V_e(f)). For integer sequences c,uc,u and a positive integer vv, the recurrence vc(n+1)=2u(n)−u(n+1)v c(n+1)=2u(n)-u(n+1) gives c=2Bu−uv+(c(0)+u(0)v)δ0.c=\frac{2Bu-u}{v}+\left(c(0)+\frac{u(0)}v\right)\delta_0. Since every section of δ0\delta_0 is 00 or δ0\delta_0, it follows that Ve(c)⊆Ve(u)+B(Ve(u))+ℚδ0,dim⁡ℚVe(c)≤2dim⁡ℚVe(u)+1.V_e(c)\subseteq V_e(u)+B(V_e(u))+\mathbb{Q}\delta_0, \qquad \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} V_e(c)\le2\dim_{\mathbb{Q}} V_e(u)+1. In particular, bounded carry ranks would force bounded coefficient ranks. Non-22-regularity of cc therefore forces unbounded carry ranks. This is an ordinary proof, not a claim of a new Lean declaration. It also gives the generic bound dim⁡ℚVe(u)≥2e−1\dim_{\mathbb{Q}} V_e(u)\ge2^{e-1} for c=φc=\varphi and e≥1e\ge1, using the coefficient rank 2e+12^e+1. The factor 22 is not an additive O(1)O(1) loss, and this bound concerns all sections, including level zero.

The theorem for φ\varphi in Proposition 1.6 is sharper: the carry sections at all residues of levels 1,…,e1,\ldots,e have rank at least 2e−12^e-1. It uses the independence of the odd-residue totient sections. Neither lower bound is an irrationality proof, since rational coefficient series can have nonregular carries. The separate 5/45/4 comparison verifies this directly. Any proposed rank upper bound must use additional totient-specific hypotheses not satisfied by the 5/45/4 comparison sequence.

Finite observations and quantified conditions

The finite observations can be compared with the quantified conditions, but they do not establish an asymptotic digit distribution. They also supply no basis for ranking possible proof methods.

Comparison of conditions.

The first four conditions concern the same constant but impose different averaging, sampling and separation requirements. The 11/10011/100 digit-change test in Corollary 12.3 is sufficient for a real-part bound; it is not a replacement for the norm or four-term rows. Only the full-depth row is proved here to be equivalent to irrationality. The last row records a false generic upper bound, not an additional open hypothesis.

Quantitative estimates.

The counterexamples identify missing assumptions in the specific arguments tested here. They do not imply that the binary digits of SS are random, normal, or unusually structured. A constructed counterexample can disprove an implication without resembling SS in other respects. Likewise, failure of one congruence construction does not exclude every use of the Chinese remainder theorem.

Additional arithmetic information.

Table [tab:blocks] records finite observations: the sampled digit-change proportions are near 0.500.50, above the sufficient threshold 0.110.11, and the displayed normalized cosine sums are below 0.890.89. These computations are compatible with the proposed conditions. They do not establish those conditions for every shift and arbitrarily large blocks, or prove a fair-coin model for the digits. The relevant quantified estimates remain unproved here.

The recorded small margins near a forbidden endpoint also require careful interpretation. One small margin disproves a proposed lower bound larger than that margin at that index. It does not rule out every positive margin on a suitable subsequence, or every estimate with scale-dependent bounds. No numerical census in this record determines which of these possibilities holds asymptotically.

Scope of the comparison.

Corollary 12.3 specifies one sufficient digit statistic: for every fixed hh, the digit-change proportion must reach at least 11/10011/100 on arbitrarily large blocks. A statement for one shift, a smaller positive proportion, or finitely many blocks is not this hypothesis. An upper bound o(N)o(N) on the longest run alone would not imply irrationality; a periodic alternating expansion has bounded runs. The prime-index condition in [eq:primefibre] is another proposed sufficient estimate. Its exact algebraic decomposition does not establish the required correlation bound.

Remaining arithmetic questions

The remaining questions ask for witnesses with unbounded indices. We collect them in residue and exponential-sum form, retaining the quantifiers needed to imply irrationality of S=∑n≥0φ(n)2−nS=\sum_{n\ge0}\varphi(n)2^{-n}. Erdős Problem #249 remains open.

This section collects quantified conditions on the scaled tail RN=∑j≥0φ(N+1+j)2−(j+1)R_N=\sum_{j\ge0}\varphi(N+1+j)2^{-(j+1)} that suffice for irrationality. The implication theorems and the arithmetic assumptions have different status: the former are proved in the indicated sources, while the latter are not supplied for the actual totient sequence. Each condition is stated with its quantifiers and linked to its formal source. The comparison distinguishes proved equivalences from one-way sufficient conditions. It is not an exhaustive list of possible methods. A finite list of certificates does not stand in for a condition beyond every threshold, and an implication does not establish its antecedent.

Recall that Ht=H(t)=lcm⁡(1,…,t)H_t=H(t)=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\dots,t) (Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.periodLcm). For fixed h,Nh,N, this excluded radius grows linearly with LL, while its proportion of the modulus tends to zero.

Certificate completeness

For each fixed h,N≥0h,N\ge0, a certificate at some unrestricted depth exists exactly when the tail difference is nonintegral: (∃L≥0,𝒞(h,N,L))⇔RN+h−RN∉ℤ.\bigl(\exists L\ge0,\ \mathcal C(h,N,L)\bigr) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad R_{N+h}-R_N\notin\mathbb Z. This equivalence removes the existential depth from the unrestricted certificate conditions below, including the diagonal and LCM-grid forms. It does not by itself supply a depth bound, a prescribed separation margin, a common depth for a family, or an exponential-sum estimate. Such requirements must be retained unless a separate argument removes them. In particular, completeness does not establish any of the quantified nonintegrality assertions needed for irrationality.

The original quantified residue condition

The threshold quantifier excludes every possible starting point for a rational tail period.

The quantified residue condition. S∉ℚ⇔∀h≥1∀N0∃N≥N0∃L,𝒞(h,N,L).S\notin\mathbb Q \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \forall h\ge1\ \forall N_0\ \exists N\ge N_0\ \exists L, \quad\mathcal C(h,N,L).

Here 𝒞(h,N,L)\mathcal C(h,N,L) is the finite residue test defined earlier; the universal quantifiers over hh and N0N_0 belong to the displayed assertion, not to that finite test. Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.irrational_totient_series_iff_certificate_supply The equivalence is proved; the quantified existence assertion is not proved.

The reverse direction is by contradiction against the tail-period law: if SS were rational, the eventual-period theorem (Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.eventual_period_of_not_irrational, unconditional) supplies a period h>0h>0 and pre-period N0N_0 with RN+h−RN∈ℤR_{N+h}-R_N\in\mathbb{Z} for all N≥N0N\ge N_0; the certificate hypothesis instantiated at that (h,N0)(h,N_0) produces an N≥N0N\ge N_0 where RN+h−RN∉ℤR_{N+h}-R_N\notin\mathbb{Z}, a contradiction via nonintegrality from a certificate (Erdos249257.TotientTailPeriodKiller.tail_diff_notMem_int_of_certifiedKill).

For the forward direction, irrationality gives pointwise non-integrality of every positive tail shift and certificate completeness supplies a witness already at N=N0N=N_0.

For fixed hh, the required certificate may choose both N≥N0N\ge N_0 and LL. It is not required at every NN or every depth. Its error radius is N+h+L+2N+h+L+2, so for fixed h,Nh,N it grows only linearly in LL, whereas the modulus is 2L2^L. The missing assertion is that an admissible residue lies outside both endpoint intervals beyond every threshold, for every positive hh. The reformulations below specify other ways to choose such witnesses; none establishes this assertion for the actual totient sequence.

A bound for an exponential sum is sufficient for the quantified residue condition. With e(x)=exp⁡(2πix)e(x)=\exp(2\pi i x), the assertion is block norm condition:≡∀h>0,∀X0,∃X,L,max⁡(X0,1)≤X∧16(2X+h+L+2)≤2L∧∥∑N∈[X,2X)e(D(h,N,L)/2L)∥≤2125X.\text{block norm condition} :\equiv\ \forall h>0,\ \forall X_0,\ \exists X,L,\quad \max(X_0,1)\le X\ \wedge\ 16\,(2X+h+L+2)\le 2^L\ \wedge\ \Bigl\|\sum_{N\in[X,2X)} e\bigl(D(h,N,L)/2^L\bigr)\Bigr\| \le \tfrac{21}{25}X. The underlying finite lemma is more general: it applies to any nonempty finite T⊆[0,2X)T\subseteq[0,2X) with the stated size bound and ∥∑N∈Te(D(h,N,L)/2L)∥≤(21/25)|T|\|\sum_{N\in T}e(D(h,N,L)/2^L)\|\le(21/25)|T|. What supplying this form would take: genuine cancellation for the additive character e(D(h,N,L)/2L)e(D(h,N,L)/2^L) at the growing dyadic moduli permitted by the size bound. Thus nonvanishing of that determinant alone cannot prove cancellation. A successful use of a determinant would need further information connecting its entries to the phase sum; the comparison does not exclude every such argument.

Five sufficient conditions for that residue inequality

Farey growth and the failed generic rank argument

The Farey growth law is an open sufficient hypothesis. The generic rank bound listed beside it is false for rational comparison sequences, and is retained to explain that failed input rather than as another open problem.

The hypothetical rank bound.

Unconditionally, for every level e≥1e\ge1, the dyadic totient basis of 2e+12^e+1 sequences is linearly independent over ℚ\mathbb{Q} (via CRT and Dirichlet’s theorem on primes in arithmetic progression) (Erdos249257.linearIndependent_canonicalTotientKernelFamily). Consequently, if S∈ℚS\in\mathbb{Q}, there is an integer v>0v>0 with vS∈ℤvS\in\mathbb{Z}. Its integral carry uN=vRNu_N=vR_N satisfies, for every e≥0e\ge0, dim⁡ℚspan⁡{n↦u2jn+r:1≤j≤e,0≤r<2j}≥2e−1.\dim_{\mathbb{Q}}\operatorname{span} \{n\mapsto u_{2^j n+r}:1\le j\le e,\ 0\le r<2^j\}\ge2^e-1. It obeys uN+1=2uN−vφ(N+1)u_{N+1}=2u_N-v\varphi(N+1) and 0≤uN≤v(N+2)0\le u_N\le v(N+2). Erdos249257.not_irrational_totientSeries_implies_unbounded_carryRank_unconditional

A bound independent of ee for these same carry-section ranks would contradict the displayed lower bound; so would an upper bound that is o(2e)o(2^e). Rationality and linear coefficient growth alone do not give either conclusion: the fixed sequence constructed in Section 12.6 has sum 5/45/4 and the same rank lower bound. An incompatible upper bound for the actual totient carry would have to use information not shared by that comparison sequence.

The most direct generic construction is also impossible: no integer certificate satisfying the following conditions (Q⋅v⋅A=boundaryQ\cdot v\cdot A = \mathrm{boundary} with |boundary|<Q⋅v|\mathrm{boundary}|<Q\cdot v and A≠0A\ne0) can exist (Erdos249257.false_of_compressedAdjointCertificate); and the full family is proved infinite-dimensional in span, the case k=2k=2 of Coons’s non-regularity theorem (§10.8; Erdos249257.not_finiteDimensional_span_fullTotientKernel).

Proposition 1.7 gives a common eventual period modulo vv for the sections of this same uu, together with their unbounded rational ranks. These conclusions concern different properties of the same carry; they supply no rank upper bound.

Growth of the Farey denominator bound.

The finite denominator exclusion for SS comes from a Farey-gap denominator exclusion at a single fixed window K=240K=240: S≠a/bfor all a∈ℤ,1≤b≤79639646646701375323355774875831053,gcd⁡(a,b)=1.S\ne a/b\quad\text{for all }a\in\mathbb{Z},\quad 1\le b\le79639646646701375323355774875831053, \quad\gcd(a,b)=1. A different window requires a new certificate or a uniform argument; the fixed-window calculation supplies neither.

A sufficient extension is a function g(K)→∞g(K)\to\infty for which every (N=1,K)(N=1,K) gap check excludes all rationals of reduced denominator at most g(K)g(K). More generally, unbounded valid exclusion bounds along a sequence of windows suffice. This is a statement about the certified intervals. The record does not prove it equivalent to a lower bound on the continued-fraction denominators of SS. This extension is unproved.

For pp prime and e≥1e\ge1, a successful unit-gap certificate at denominator pep^e has zero candidates or a single candidate divisible by pp (Erdos249257.reducedDenominatorCandidateCount_prime_pow_le_one). The success hypothesis is essential: the bound is not a statement about every window at that denominator. Nor does it bound the eventual denominator cutoff. The prime-power restriction cannot be omitted, as the modulo-1515 example in Observation 6.114 shows. No obstruction to a uniform estimate as KK varies is proved here.

Summary of implications

For each condition, the second column states its relation to the quantified residue test or to the named intermediate assertion.

Reading the table. “Sufficient” records only the indicated implication. It does not assert a converse or a strict comparison of strength. “Equivalent” records two proved directions, either directly or through the base equivalence with S∉ℚS\notin\mathbb Q. Logical equivalence does not by itself provide a direct construction from the finite witnesses in one formulation to those in another.

Remaining estimates

Two explicit estimates for φ\varphi remain: weighted cancellation in the exponential sums and a residue inequality involving the final totient difference. Neither is derived here from the cited methods. Other approaches to the irrationality question are not excluded.

Exponential sums.

For each fixed h>0h>0 and every threshold X0X_0, the block norm condition asks for some X≥max⁡(X0,1)X\ge\max(X_0,1) and LL satisfying both the modulus bound and |∑N∈[X,2X)e(D(h,N,L)/2L)|≤2125X.\left|\sum_{N\in[X,2X)}e\bigl(D(h,N,L)/2^L\bigr)\right| \le\frac{21}{25}X. The saving 21/2521/25 is fixed, but the chosen block and depth may depend on hh and X0X_0; uniformity of these choices in hh is not required. The preceding four-term decomposition and the proved counting bounds identify contributions to this sum. By Theorem 3.5(b) the two remaining weighted estimates may be replaced by the single bound Re⁡∑N∈𝒢E(h,N,L(X))≤603X/1000\operatorname{Re}\sum_{N\in\mathcal G}E(h,N,L(X))\le603X/1000 at s=26s=26, η=1/1000\eta=1/1000 and minimal depth, for arbitrarily large XX; that bound is open. The record therefore gives an exact reduction and some of its estimates; the displayed cancellation bound remains unproved.

The last totient difference.

The endpoint criteria compare δ2a(2q+2)=φ(2H+2q+2)−φ(H+2q+2),H=H2a,\delta_{2^a}(2q+2) =\varphi(2H+2q+2)-\varphi(H+2q+2),\qquad H=H_{2^a}, with twice the centred residue ua,qu_{a,q}. An appropriate inequality, proved for arbitrarily large aa with the stated bounds on qq, would contradict the carry interval required by integrality. The exact identity explains why such an inequality would suffice; it does not supply the inequality. The finite examples through t=82t=82, and the short-window examples at a=4,6a=4,6, do not establish an asymptotic pattern.

Complementary proofs for the short paper

The basis theorem, the integral relation theorem and the bounded residue theorem have complete proofs in the short paper. This appendix supplies the longer arguments behind its discussion of SS: propagation from a nonintegral tail, Mersenne residues, rational comparisons and the sharp rank-one bound. Throughout, K(h,N,L)K(h,N,L) is the residue condition 𝒞(h,N,L)\mathcal C(h,N,L) defined in the main text.

Residues modulo divisors of Mersenne numbers

The test below asks whether the residue of −BH,c-B_{H,c} stays away from the endpoints by more than the tail error.

Equivalent formulation A.2 (A residue test modulo a divisor of 2H−12^H-1). The series SS is irrational if and only if, for every c≥0c\ge0 and odd v≥1v\ge1, some positive multiple HH of φ(v)\varphi(v) satisfies c+H+1<(−BH,c)mod⁡M<M−(c+H+1).\begin{equation} \label{eq:canonical-gap} c+H+1<(-B_{H,c})\operatorname{mod} M<M-(c+H+1). \end{equation}

Proof. The identity BH,c=2HRc−Rc+H=M(vRc)−ΔH(c)B_{H,c}=2^HR_c-R_{c+H}=M(vR_c)-\Delta_H(c) is exact. For H≥1H\ge1, |ΔH(c)|<c+H+1|\Delta_H(c)|<c+H+1. Indeed RN≤N+1R_N\le N+1 for N≥1N\ge1 and 0<R0≤3/20<R_0\le3/2; the strict inequalities follow by subtracting a positive tail. If S=a/(2cv)S=a/(2^cv), then vRc∈ℤvR_c\in\mathbb{Z} and ΔH(c)∈ℤ\Delta_H(c)\in\mathbb{Z}. The residue of −BH,c-B_{H,c} is therefore within distance less than c+H+1c+H+1 of 0(mod⁡M)0\pmod M, so [eq:canonical-gap] fails.

If SS is irrational, fix c,vc,v. Then vRcvR_c is nonintegral. As HH tends to infinity through positive multiples of φ(v)\varphi(v), ΔH(c)/M→0\Delta_H(c)/M\to0 and (c+H+1)/M→0(c+H+1)/M\to0. Hence the fractional part of −BH,c/M=−vRc+ΔH(c)/M-B_{H,c}/M=-vR_c+\Delta_H(c)/M stays away from both endpoints of [0,1][0,1], which gives [eq:canonical-gap] for all sufficiently large such HH. ◻

With its universal quantifiers, this condition is equivalent to the unresolved irrationality assertion. A rational value a/(2cv)a/(2^cv) fails the test for that same c,vc,v, whereas irrationality gives it for every sufficiently large allowed HH. The proof does not find such an HH without assuming irrationality.

A formal declaration for the equivalence is available here, with the modulus written as vM=2H−1vM=2^H-1. The finite residues also satisfy ρH,N+1,M=(2ρH,N,M−φ(N+H+1)+φ(N+1))mod⁡M,ρH,N,M=(−BH,N)mod⁡M,\rho_{H,N+1,M}= \bigl(2\rho_{H,N,M}-\varphi(N+H+1)+\varphi(N+1)\bigr)\operatorname{mod} M, \quad \rho_{H,N,M}=(-B_{H,N})\operatorname{mod} M, which is an exact recurrence for searches directed at [eq:canonical-gap].

LCM tails and rational comparisons

We first specialise the tail congruence to LCM shifts, then compare it with rational series preserving selected coefficient data. The source declarations accompany the formulas; references point to the complete constructions and their hypotheses in the preceding sections.

  1. Tail differences at least common multiples. Let Ha=lcm⁡(1,…,2a)H_a=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,2^a). Then SS is irrational if and only if, beyond every threshold a0a_0, some a≥a0a\ge a_0 satisfies ΔHa(Ha)∉ℤ\Delta_{H_a}(H_a)\notin\mathbb{Z}. This is the exact cofinal nonintegrality criterion for the actual LCM diagonal, not a quantitative separation estimate and not a proof that such indices occur; the forward implication is recorded separately.

  2. Positive tail differences need not be nonintegral. For a≥8a\ge8 and J+(a+6)<2⋅2aJ+(a+6)<2\cdot2^a, one has ΔHa(Ha+J)>0\Delta_{H_a}(H_a+J)>0. Suppose this difference is an integer. If a truncation depth KK satisfies J+K+(a+6)<2⋅2a,2Ha+J+K+2<2K,J+K+(a+6)<2\cdot2^a, \qquad 2H_a+J+K+2<2^K, then DHa,Ha+J,Kmod⁡2K=2K−ΔHa(Ha+J+K)D_{H_a,H_a+J,K}\operatorname{mod}2^K =2^K-\Delta_{H_a}(H_a+J+K) lies strictly between 2K−(2Ha+J+K+2)2^K-(2H_a+J+K+2) and 2K2^K. The later tail difference is a positive integer; its negative is the representative near zero. Thus positivity determines which endpoint contains the residue, but does not exclude an integral tail difference. Both displayed bounds on KK are required for this conclusion. Source declarations: positive tail differences, negative endpoint representative, residue near the upper endpoint.

  3. Divisibility and finite linear combinations do not suffice. A dyadic coboundary is a sequence of the form 2uj−uj+12u_j-u_{j+1}; its weighted sum telescopes. For every t≥3t\ge3, with H=lcm⁡(1,…,t)H=\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,t), the linked source constructs a nonzero comparison sequence of this form. Its coefficients reproduce the actual totient differences at t−2t-2 prescribed indices and are divisible by φ(H)\varphi(H). Every finite integer linear combination of forward shifts preserves the telescoping identity and divisibility by φ(H)\varphi(H) and the corresponding lower-level factors. The bounds remain uniform in the index, but are multiplied by the sum of the absolute values of the combination’s coefficients. A variant preserves sparse prescribed values along entire arithmetic progressions. These properties alone do not force a contradiction: the comparison need not consist of actual totient differences. The theorem concerns linear combinations of shifts, not nonlinear operations, and does not supply certificates at arbitrarily large scales. Source declarations: obstruction for finite integer combinations of shifts.

If S=a/vS=a/v with integers aa and v≥1v\ge1, the scaled tails uN=vRNu_N=vR_N are integers and satisfy uN+1=2uN−vφ(N+1),0≤uN≤v(N+2).u_{N+1}=2u_N-v\varphi(N+1),\qquad 0\le u_N\le v(N+2). In particular uN/2N→0u_N/2^N\to0. Its dyadic sections n↦u2jn+rn\mapsto u_{2^jn+r} have rational rank at least 2e−12^e-1 through level ee and a common eventual period modulo vv. Both properties are the corresponding theorem for the same carry; they are compatible, and neither supplies a contradiction.

Section 12.6 constructs a rational comparison sequence with c(n)=φ(n)c(n)=\varphi(n) for odd nn, |c(n)−φ(n)|≤2|c(n)-\varphi(n)|\le2 for even nn, 0≤c(n)≤n0\le c(n)\le n, and ∑n≥1c(n)2−n=54.\sum_{n\ge1}c(n)2^{-n}=\frac54. This comparison sequence has an integral carry satisfying uN/2N→0u_N/2^N\to0, with dyadic rank at least 2e−12^e-1 at every level. Thus the same lower bound for a hypothetical totient carry is compatible with rationality. For one fixed prime pp and g:ℕ→ℤg:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}, the exact laws g(pn)=pg(n)g(pn)=p g(n) when p∣np\mid n and g(pn)=(p−1)g(n)g(pn)=(p-1)g(n) otherwise, together with g−φ=o(n)g-\varphi=o(n), force g=φg=\varphi: a nonzero defect keeps a nonzero ratio to the argument along pjnp^j n. The comparison sequence fails these dilation laws. The unchanged odd-residue sections also give coefficient rank at least 2e−12^e-1 at every level. This is a lower bound, not an exact formula for the full coefficient rank.

The sharp rank-one quotient bound

The quotients below are a particular proposed family of rational approximants to a Möbius-weighted value. We determine their minimum and show that they remain a fixed distance above that value. Put Θ2=∑d≥1μ(d)(2d−1)2=S−12,Q(e,Y)=(∑d=1Yμ(d)/(2d−1)e+2)2∑d=1Yμ(d)/(2d−1)2e+2.\Theta_2=\sum_{d\ge1}\frac{\mu(d)}{(2^d-1)^2}=S-\frac12, \qquad Q(e,Y)=\frac{\bigl(\sum_{d=1}^{Y}\mu(d)/(2^d-1)^{e+2}\bigr)^2} {\sum_{d=1}^{Y}\mu(d)/(2^d-1)^{2e+2}}. The divisor-convolution identity φ=μ*Id\varphi=\mu*\mathrm{Id} gives S=∑d≥1μ(d)2d/(2d−1)2S=\sum_{d\ge1}\mu(d)2^d/(2^d-1)^2. Now 2d=(2d−1)+12^d=(2^d-1)+1 and ∑d≥1μ(d)/(2d−1)=1/2\sum_{d\ge1}\mu(d)/(2^d-1)=1/2, the latter following from ∑d∣nμ(d)=0\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)=0 for n>1n>1 and 11 for n=1n=1. These identities give the displayed value of Θ2\Theta_2; all the sums are absolutely convergent. Amiram Eldar posted the corresponding formula S=12+∑d≥1μ(d)/(2d−1)2S=\tfrac12+\sum_{d\ge1}\mu(d)/(2^d-1)^2, together with its coprimality interpretation, to OEIS A256936 on 15 March 2026 [8], and Steve Fan posted the formula on the problem’s forum thread on 16 May 2026 [9]. The result below gives the exact extremum for this family, refining the earlier lower bound 1/4801/480 in Section 6.6.13.

It remains to compare the minimum with Θ2\Theta_2. An upper bound for Θ2\Theta_2 proves the stated gap; a lower bound disproves the stronger proposed gap. The same tail estimate at r=2r=2 gives P6(2)−13072≤Θ2≤P7(2)+112288.P_6(2)-\frac1{3072}\le\Theta_2\le P_7(2)+\frac1{12288}. Direct fraction comparison, using P6(2)=3309559/3814209P_6(2)=3309559/3814209 and P7(2)=53376062902/61519376961P_7(2)=53376062902/61519376961, yields q*−(P7(2)+112288)>21320,q*−(P6(2)−13072)<115.q_*-\left(P_7(2)+\frac1{12288}\right)>\frac{21}{320}, \qquad q_*-\left(P_6(2)-\frac1{3072}\right)<\frac1{15}. Multiplying the strict lower gap by positive weights, summing over a nonempty finite set and dividing by the positive total weight proves the assertion for weighted averages. ◻

This theorem treats averages after the quotients are formed. Signed coefficients, coupling before the quotient, and higher-rank kernels require separate arguments. For rational approximants pj/qjp_j/q_j in lowest terms, with qj>0q_j>0, a sufficient arithmetic target is 0<qj|Θ2−pj/qj|→0.0<q_j\left|\Theta_2-p_j/q_j\right|\longrightarrow0. The denominator sets the scale of the required error. Convergence alone does not control their product. For the elementary dyadic prefixes, the available bound is only qj|S−pj/qj|≤N+2q_j|S-p_j/q_j|\le N+2 at depth NN, not a quantity tending to zero. A prescribed approximation family therefore needs a sharper error or reduced-denominator bound. When approximants may be chosen freely, continued-fraction convergents show that the criterion is equivalent to irrationality, just as [eq:canonical-gap] is. The theorem above excludes the displayed rank-one quotients and their positive averages, not other approximation families.

Declarations

Further background.

Erick Wong posted a proof that ∑n≥1(φ(n)mod⁡k)k−n\sum_{n\ge1}(\varphi(n)\operatorname{mod} k)k^{-n} is irrational for every integer k>2k>2 on Mathematics Stack Exchange on 29 March 2015 [5]; there the base equals the modulus. Erdős’s 1957 criterion already gives every base (Remark 1.13). The Möbius-square form of SS and its coprimality interpretation were posted publicly before this record, as credited in §5.4. Kovač and Tao show that suitable subsums of Lambert series in distinct integer bases can be rational ; the freedom to choose those subsums is absent for SS. The Lambert-series factorisations of Merca [17] and of Merca and Schmidt  are transform background for the Möbius–Mersenne coordinate. Balasubramanian, Giri and Srivastav prove asymptotics for finite shifted convolutions of divisor-convolution functions, including φ(n)/n\varphi(n)/n, uniformly for |h|≤x/2|h|\le x/2 at cutoff xx . Their partial-summation extension uses differentiable weights with bounded derivative on the summation interval [19]. Applying that observation here would require control of the weighted error for the present phases; no such estimate is established in this record. The cited results are not themselves the dyadic residue separation required by Sep\mathrm{Sep}. The remaining sources are cited where their hypotheses are used.

At the generating-function level, the published height criterion of Adamczewski, Bell and Smertnig gives kk-regularity for a kk-Mahler series with integer coefficients of polynomial growth  . For the totient coefficients the logarithmic heights are log⁡max⁡(1,φ(n))≤log⁡n\log\max(1,\varphi(n))\le\log n for n≥1n\ge1, so Coons’s nonregularity already rules out kk-Mahler equations in every base. The later multiplicative classification of Bell and Smertnig provides another route [32]. The algebraic and DD-finite classifications of Bell, Bruin and Coons belong to the same function-level context [33]. They do not by themselves decide the value at z=1/2z=1/2.

Automatic prime-sampling theorems address a different issue. Adamczewski, Drmota and Müllner identify a computable local coprimality condition governing the relevant logarithmic densities, with a conditional ordinary-density transfer [34]. Their theorem does not assert that every output state has positive density on a prescribed prime progression, nor does it prove independence with automatic coefficient weights. Any use for that purpose needs its own compatibility argument.

It does not check that every prose summary has the same hypotheses or verify the literature comparisons. In particular, a checked implication with an unproved hypothesis is not a proof that Problem 249 is solved.
